Check off sessions in the Weekly Plan tab. 40 sessions over 8 weeks.
The weekly rhythm. Same structure repeats for all 8 weeks — what changes each block is the load and volume (see the Lifting and Conditioning tabs).
Mon
Lift A
Tue
Sprints
Wed
Rest / walk
Thu
Lift B
Fri
Tempo + Agility
Sat
Lift C
Sun
Rest
Why 5 days, not 3
You're sitting most of the day driving, so the biggest miss in the old plan was that nothing built your aerobic base — the thing that actually stops you from gassing out in the second half. The tempo/agility day fixes that. Sprints handle short bursts, tempo running handles the engine underneath them.
Session tracker
Your scale's BMR read 1,757 kcal. A driving job with occasional walking puts real maintenance closer to 2,300–2,400. This targets a steady ~450–500 cal/day deficit — about 1 lb/week — without wrecking training or work energy.
1,850calories
165gprotein
175gcarbs
55gfat
100ozwater
The beer math, for the record
A regular six-pack runs 900–1,000+ calories, and your body burns off the alcohol before it touches stored fat — so the deficit pauses while that's happening. Cutting it out is worth more to the belly and love handles specifically than anything in the workouts. Everything else here is secondary to that one change.
Working around a driving job
  1. Prep meals the night before in a cooler bag — protein, a carb source, veggies. Route stops make fresh cooking impossible mid-shift.
  2. Keep jerky, protein bars, or nuts in the cab for the moments you're stuck and hungry, instead of gas station food.
  3. Sitting most of the day dulls thirst cues. Keep a bottle up front and refill on your walking stops — those 10x/hour walks are a good trigger to sip.
  4. Reassess after 2 weeks. If the scale hasn't moved, drop calories another 100–150, don't drop them further right away.
Same three workouts all 8 weeks, but the load climbs every 2 weeks. Pick the block that matches where you are.
Workout A
Monday — Lower Body + Core
Workout B
Thursday — Upper Push/Pull + Core
Workout C
Saturday — Full Body Circuit
How to run Workout C
This one's a circuit, not straight sets — it's the metabolic finisher for the week. Move through all 5 exercises back to back with only 30–45s rest between them, then rest 90s and repeat for the listed rounds.
Two conditioning days a week. Sprints build your top-end burst, tempo + agility builds the engine that keeps you sharp late in games.
Sprint Day — Repeated Sprint Ability
Tuesday
  1. Jog easy for 5 minutes to warm up
  2. Sprint hard for 30 seconds
  3. Walk to recover — length shrinks each block, see table below
  4. Repeat sprint + walk for the block's total reps
  5. Walk 5 minutes to cool down
BlockWalk restTotal sprints
Weeks 1–290 sec8
Weeks 3–475 sec8
Weeks 5–660 sec8
Weeks 7–845 sec10
Tempo + Agility Day
Friday
  1. 5 min easy jog to warm up
  2. Agility drills — 3 sets each of: in-and-out steps, lateral shuffle, high knees, backpedal (ladder or just marked lines on grass work)
  3. 20 min continuous jog at a conversational pace — this is the aerobic base that prevents the second-half fade
  4. 5x 20-yard shuttle sprints — sprint, plant, sprint back, this is the change-of-direction work soccer actually demands
  5. 5 min walk to cool down
⚠️ Keep at least one rest or light day between Sprint Day and Tempo/Agility Day. Back-to-back hard conditioning days without recovery is how you start regressing instead of progressing.
Beer was the actual leak here. The workouts build the muscle and the conditioning builds the engine, but the deficit is what lets the belly and love handles actually show what's underneath. Keep the calories honest and the beer out, and the rest of this does its job.
